body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{jh}(w)=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{j,T_j+h}-\sum_{i\in D_{jh}}w_{jh,i}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,T_j+h}\), with honest-width frontier \(W_s\) and fixed-Bonferroni SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) for \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\)

sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed integer dimensions, deterministic adoption dates with \(\mathcal J\ne\varnothing\), rational predictors and class radii, a known rational covariance factor, and a certified rational Bonferroni multiplier.
sampling_model.units: The finite set \(\mathcal I\) contains treated, not-yet-treated, and never-treated units; repeated unit--calendar-time cells are deduplicated in \(Q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and deterministic; \(D_{jh}=\{i:T_i>T_j+h\}\) identifies untreated donor outcomes at the relevant calendar time.
sampling_model.overlap: The treated set is nonempty, and every deepest donor pool \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty; nesting then makes every horizon-specific donor simplex feasible and gives \(M\geq1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs. For general \(L\) and \(\delta\), exact robustness maximizes the shifted Gaussian-cube radius over the compact joint image of the shared coefficient balls and cellwise remainder box; it does not combine coordinatewise bias endpoints. Correlated Gaussian probability evaluation and numerical max calibration remain post-solve computational refinements. The fixed-Bonferroni SOCP is the directly conic implementation, and the diagonal row-disjoint zero-bias specialization reduces exact calibration to one product equation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper defines shrinking not-yet-treated donor sets and focuses its exposition and application on the common deepest-horizon pool, while explicitly noting that its estimator may instead use horizon-varying donor sets; it does not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class or evaluate the width programs here.
The paper offers non-asymptotic staggered synthetic-control prediction intervals, conic implementations, and uniform inference across post-treatment periods.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for scalar linear functionals over convex regression classes under known-variance Gaussian errors.
The paper trades worst-case conditional imbalance against variance when constructing generalized optimal matching weights.
The paper constructs facial-reduced extended duals with strong duality when ordinary conic constraint qualifications fail.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient closed-cone conditions for Farkas lemmas and strong duality in second-order-cone programming.

body.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking not-yet-treated donor sets. Conditional on the declared nonempty rational fixed design, this note maps every treated-unit--horizon error into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector and defines the jointly attainable bias set generated by the shared calendar-time coefficients and cellwise remainder bounds. The exact honest deterministic linear-band frontier is the attained minimum, over the relevant product of donor simplexes, of the worst shifted Gaussian-cube radius over that joint bias set. A fixed-Bonferroni bias-plus-standard-error SOCP remains finite-sample honest and within the stated dimension-uniform spectral factor of this exact frontier. A legal common-donor family with rational covariance factor proves that the square-root covariance-condition-number dependence is order-sharp for fixed Bonferroni calibration. Zero-bias Loewner and diagonal row-disjoint results still give computable strict nested-width gains, while the facial-reduction theorem separately certifies strict improvement of the SOCP surrogate on degenerate faces. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein provide donor geometry only; \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are implementation consumers, not estimators covered by these theorems.

project_justification.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein define the shrinking donor geometry and discuss deepest-pool and horizon-varying choices, but they do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance experiment or an honest-width frontier for their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik provide non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction and conic architecture, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik provide the closely related synthetic-control prediction-interval setting; neither gives the exact min--max shifted Gaussian-cube frontier over jointly constrained biases or the order-sharp comparison with fixed Bonferroni calibration. The nearby weight-robust literature addresses different operations: Kallus optimizes a bias--variance matching criterion, Cerulli studies initial donor selection, and Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang use placebo-in-time bootstrap calibration. None is a transfer theorem for this declared deterministic-weight, known-covariance simultaneous rectangle. Scalar convex-class interval theory does not resolve that correlated rectangle or its donor-support comparison.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance in a prespecified positive spectral band, rational fixed inputs, a nonempty treated set, and this note's bounded linear conditional-mean class define a finite-sample decision problem in which donor availability, shared-cell covariance, joint bias attainability, multiplicity, and exact width are all explicit. The targets are the exact robust frontier \(W_s\), the implementable fixed-Bonferroni SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\), strict nested-support comparisons on proved domains, and the worst-case price of the Bonferroni surrogate.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the deduplicated Gaussian contrast law and exact coordinate bias support function, proves finite-sample SOCP coverage, and characterizes the full bounded-mean frontier as an attained minimum over weights of a maximum shifted Gaussian-cube radius over the joint attainable bias set. It proves the earlier spectral comparison and constructs a legal common-donor sequence on which the SOCP-to-exact-width ratio grows as the square root of the covariance condition number. Separate zero-bias Loewner, independent-coordinate product-root, rational witness, and degeneracy-safe facial-reduction results identify when nested supports strictly improve the exact frontier or its SOCP surrogate.

body.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2) supply the shrinking not-yet-treated donor-set geometry and note that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors even though their exposition and application focus on a common deepest pool; they do not supply this bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide staggered prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closely related synthetic-control prediction-interval setting; neither work supplies the jointly attainable-bias shifted-Gaussian-cube min--max frontier or its order-sharp fixed-Bonferroni comparison. Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026) are relevant staggered-adoption synthetic-control inference, but their application-specific procedure is not this fixed-design width program. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class, and Armstrong and Kolesar (2020) provide simple honest intervals in nonparametric regression; neither resolves this simultaneous correlated rectangle over nested donor simplexes. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance weighting analogy, but does not give uniform Gaussian-rectangle coverage or this donor-support frontier. Cerulli (2024) studies initial donor selection, whereas the present weights are deterministic and restricted by each horizon's already eligible donor set. Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang (2026) study bias-aware synthetic-control intervals calibrated by a placebo-in-time bootstrap; that is distinct from the declared known-covariance Gaussian experiment and its exact robust width. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015) provide Gaussian-max comparison and anti-concentration tools, not this weight optimization or joint bias set. Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supplies the weak moving-set inequality used by the separate strict zero-bias Loewner result. Pataki (2013) supplies minimal-face strong duality, and Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008) supply SOCP-duality context; neither gives this nested-primal versus deep-facial-dual, algebraic interval-separated strict-gap certificate. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the real-algebraic elimination and sign-determination substrate used to construct that certificate, not a conic-support comparison. The present results retain the declared known-covariance experiment; they do not claim a covariance-estimation or published-class transfer theorem. \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are named as potential software consumers of the geometry and optimization, not as covered procedures.
body.interpretation: The exact full-class formula keeps the bias coordinates coupled through common calendar-time coefficients and deduplicated cell remainders. This matters because the endpoint attaining one coordinate's bias need not attain all other endpoints simultaneously; the robust width is therefore a maximum over the attainable joint image, not over a Cartesian bias box. In the order-sharp family, every treated contrast shares one donor shock while its treated-cell shock is independent and much smaller. The shared shock keeps the exact Gaussian maximum bounded on the donor-noise scale even when the number of treated units is exponential in the covariance condition number, whereas fixed Bonferroni calibration still pays a square-root log-multiplicity factor. The earlier strict witness continues to isolate the value of an early donor that remains untreated only at the early horizon. These conclusions concern deterministic linear bands in the declared experiment, not the numerical output or statistical class of an existing synthetic-control estimator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact full-class characterization is a finite-dimensional attained min--max functional, but evaluating correlated shifted Gaussian-cube probabilities and globally optimizing that generally nonconic objective can be computationally harder than solving the Bonferroni SOCP. The order-sharp family shows that the square-root spectral condition-number loss of fixed Bonferroni calibration cannot be removed uniformly, although particular covariance and donor geometries may yield a much smaller gap. The covariance remains known and prespecified; covariance estimation, selective donor choice, outcome-dependent weights, and transfer to a published estimator class are outside this version. The facial-reduction equivalence concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate faces and is not a general strict-\(W\) criterion.
body.honest_scope: Finite-sample SOCP coverage, the exact full bounded-mean attainable-bias frontier, the covariance-domination sandwich, its square-root condition-number order-sharpness, weak nested-support dominance, and the rational strict witnesses are theorem-level results. The exact formula uses all existing \(L\) and \(\delta\) values and maximizes over the jointly attainable bias set; it does not assume simultaneous coordinatewise endpoint attainment. On the zero-bias class, \texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier} additionally gives a strict Loewner covariance criterion, while \texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier} gives the explicit product root. The complete finite certificate \texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate} concerns strict SOCP improvement on degenerate faces. Unknown covariance, covariance confidence sets, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, direct coverage claims for the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein estimator, and coverage claims for \texttt{scpi} or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are outside the paper. Correlated Gaussian-max numerical calibration is a post-solve refinement.
